inverse: A local prediction is noninjective: degree-zero fitting sees only local mean, so zero-sum changes within a window leave its prediction unchanged. With w=n and d=0 all outputs repeat global mean; [1,-1,0] and [0,0,0] are indistinguishable for w=3. w=1,d=0 is real identity. Global smoothing is not universally invertible.
